The Redlich– Kwong–Soave with Boston–Mathias correction (RKS-BM) equation of state was used throughout much of the process simulation for high temperature, high pressure gas and liquid phase behavior. The non-random, two-liquid (NRTL) option with ideal gas properties was used for alcohol separation calculations. The ASME 1967 steam table correlations were used for the steam cycle calculations. The ELECNRTL package was used to model the electrolyte species in the quench water system. The physical solvent absorption system and the ammonia-water absorption refrigeration system were modeled in separate simulations and their results were incorporated into the main model. The perturbed-chain statistical associating fluid theory (PCSAFT) package was used to model physical solvent (DEPG) absorption processes in a separate simulation. 3 Process Design and Key Assumptions The process design for MAS and RG production comprises eight distinct modeled areas: • Area 100: Feed handling and preparation • Area 200: Gasification • Area 300: Gas quench, scrubbing, and compression • Area 400: Mixed alcohol synthesis • Area 500: Alcohol separation • Area 1100: Gas clean up and methanation • Area 700: Integrated steam system and power generation cycle • Area 800: Cooling water and other utilities A high-level block flow diagram showing the connectivity of each area is provided in Figure 6. Key assumptions and operation conditions are summarized for each area in the subsections below. 16 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nrel.gov/publications. Simplified block flow diagram for the forest residue gasification process 3.1 Area 100: Feed Handling and Drying For the purposes of this analysis, it is assumed that the plant will operate exclusively on forest residue feedstocks as motivated by the legislative actions across California and the California Energy Commission (CEC) to promote healthy forests, mitigate wildfire disasters, and generate sustainable products. The ultimate analysis for the feed considered in this study is presented in Table 7. The assumed moisture content of the biomass feedstock prior to drying is 35 wt % at the plant gate, with an additional 5 wt % moisture loss during in-plant processing. The design capacity for this study is 2,000 dry metric tonnes per day (2,205 dry tons per day), which matches that of previous NREL design reports for ethanol processes. With an expected 7,884 operating hours per year (90% on- stream factor / availability), the annual feedstock requirement is approximately 657,000 dry metric tonnes per year (724,000 dry tons per year).
